You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report describes an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in the method appendFixedWidthPadRight of the StrBuilder class. The source code of the method was inspected. The method attempts to append a string representation of an object right-padded to a fixed width, using a padding character.

The method works as follows:

1. It first checks if the requested width is greater than zero.
2. It ensures sufficient capacity in the internal buffer to hold the size plus width characters.
3. It obtains the string to append (from the object or nullText).
4. It checks the length of this string.
5. If the string length is greater than or equal to the desired width, it copies the entire string into the buffer starting at the current size position.
6. Otherwise, it copies the string into the buffer starting at the current size position, then fills the remaining space up to the width with the padChar.
7. The size is then incremented by the full width.

The bug report highlights an issue with the call str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size) when strLen >= width. The problem is that if strLen > width, copying strLen characters into buffer starting at size will overwrite beyond the space allocated for width characters, thus causing a buffer overrun and an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

The proper behavior when strLen > width should be to copy only width characters instead of strLen, so that the buffer only gets overwritten within the bounds ensured for width characters. This would mean changing the call to str.getChars(0, width, buffer, size) when strLen >= width.

Hence, the cause of the bug is that the method copies more characters than the intended width when the original string is longer than the desired fixed width.

This matches the test failure, as the test uses a StrBuilder of small initial size and tries to append "foo" with width 1 in right-padded mode, triggering the out-of-bounds error when copying 3 characters to a space reserved for 1.

Therefore, the root cause is that the appendFixedWidthPadRight method incorrectly copies the entire string when strLen >= width instead of only width characters into the buffer, causing a buffer overflow. The fix would be to copy only width characters in this condition.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(java.lang.Object,int,char)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
